_comment: flint-vs-knfsd differential floors. A regression is the RATIO falling,
not the MiB/s falling: the rig is a 2-vCPU VM on a laptop and its
absolute numbers are not comparable across time. knfsd is measured in
the same session, interleaved per rep, so rig drift is common-mode.
PROVENANCE. Two independent full runs, 2026-08-28, on lima
flint-nfs-client (Ubuntu 6.8.0 aarch64, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB), host idle,
flint-pnfs-mds 1.3.0 built from the tree at that date, mode standalone
with the sqlite state backend (the posture the hub ships).
dimension   run1    run2    ratio drift
The absolutes drifted 4-6% between those runs while the ratios drifted
under 3% -- which is the evidence for gating on the ratio at all.
Floors are the LOWER of the two runs, so a baseline fluke cannot make
the gate stricter than the rig can sustain.
TOLERANCE 0.15, not the 0.25 default: two runs put the run-to-run
spread near 3%, so 15% is ~5x the observed noise and still catches a
regression a quarter the size the old default would have. Tune it DOWN
with more runs, never up. If this gate starts crying wolf, add runs and
re-derive -- do not widen the band.
FALSIFIABILITY (this is what makes the numbers above mean anything):
a deliberately crippled mount (rsize/wsize 4096) scored read 0.088 and
write 0.119, against floors of 0.390 and 0.514. The gate sees it. The
knfsd control moved <6% across the same pair, so that collapse is the
server arm, not the rig. meta is barely affected by rsize (0.574) and
is NOT expected to fail on the crippled arm.
NOT A CLAIM ABOUT FLINT'S SPEED. read 0.459 means flint's read path is
~2.18x slower than the kernel's on this rig. That is a real, controlled
gap and the largest of the three -- but it is a FLOOR TO HOLD, not a
target that has been accepted as good.
CONTROL HEALTH. control_mib_s records what KNFSD measured when this
baseline was taken (medians of the two runs: read 1585/1488,
write 715/741, meta 1592/1582). knfsd does not change when flint
does, so if the control drifts outside +/-30% the RIG moved, and a
ratio from it is not comparable. That matters because saturation
compresses the ratio toward 1.0: a contended run reports a BETTER
ratio and would hide a regression. Observed 2026-08-28 -- a runaway
logind halved the VM and read 'improved' 0.46 -> 0.93 with no code
change at all.
